hook: Mineart began as a mechanical engineer at Caterpillar in 1999 and spent nearly three decades rising through engineering, product strategy, and electric power leadership roles before being named Chief Technology Officer, now leading Cat Technology's push to integrate smarter, more connected machines across Caterpillar's global equipment lines.
name: Jaime Mineart

quote.text: We don't just build smarter machines, we create integrated, scalable solutions that deliver real-world results.
quote.context: Jaime Mineart, personal LinkedIn profile summary

reading.body:
Jaime Mineart's path to Caterpillar's top technology role ran almost entirely through electric power, making him a notable figure at the intersection of industrial equipment and the energy infrastructure that AI data centers depend on.

Mineart joined Caterpillar in 1999 as a mechanical engineer and spent his first seventeen years in engineering before moving into product strategy for large diesel and electric power systems in 2016. His subsequent roles, each stepping up in scope, focused specifically on electric power and the commercial challenges of energy transition. By the time he became CTO in 2025, his entire senior career had been organized around power generation and delivery, not equipment broadly. That concentration matters because Caterpillar is a major supplier of backup generation and power systems to large facilities, including data centers, where reliable power is a physical prerequisite for compute at scale.

What the data does not establish is how Mineart's technology strategy will specifically address AI infrastructure demand, what products or investments fall under his current mandate, or whether Caterpillar has made any formal commitments in that direction. His background in electric power systems and energy transition commercial strategy is relevant context, but the data supports only the career record, not any conclusions about future product direction.
